title: Zirid dynasty
capsule: The Zirids were a Sanhaja Berber dynasty founded by Buluggin ibn Ziri as governors for the Fatimid Caliphate in Ifriqiya in 972; they effectively ruled independently after 1048, when al-Mu'izz ibn Badis renounced Shi'a Islam and recognized the Sunni Abbasid caliph, provoking the Fatimids to unleash the Banu Hilal and Banu Sulaym Arab tribes in devastating migrations across North Africa. The Hilalian invasions fragmented Zirid power, reducing them to the coastal city of Mahdia, and in 1148 the Norman Kingdom of Sicily under Roger II seized Mahdia, extinguishing the dynasty. The Zirids had presided over a cultural florescence at Kairouan before their collapse, and the parallel Zirid branch in al-Andalus (the Zirid taifa of Granada) was a distinct dynasty ending in 1090.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Zirid control of coastal Ifriqiya is well documented in Arabic chronicles (Ibn Khaldun, al-Tijani); their effective inland extent after the Hilalian migrations of the 1050s–1060s is much harder to map precisely.
